## Variational Inference for DGPs {#sec-dgp-variational}

In @sec-gp-variational we saw how standard GP inference is tractable due to the Gaussian conjugacy between the GP prior and the likelihood, which allows us to compute the marginal likelihood and posterior in closed form. This breaks in DGPs because the intermediate layer outputs $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$ become inputs to the next layer's kernel function $k^{(\ell)}(\vF^{(\ell-1)}, \vF^{(\ell-1)'})$, meaning the covariance matrices $K^{(\ell)}$ depend non-linearly on the random variables $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$. When we attempt to marginalise over intermediate layers, we face integrals of the form $\int \mathcal{N}(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vzero, K^{(\ell)}(\vF^{(\ell-1)})) p(\vF^{(\ell-1)}) \, d\vF^{(\ell-1)}$ where the covariance itself is a random function of the integration variable which breaks the Gaussian conjugacy that makes single-layer GPs tractable, as the resulting marginal is no longer Gaussian. To train DGPs, we need to use the variational approximations shown for single-layer GPs.


For an $L$-layer DGP, let $\vZ^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{m_\ell \times d_{\ell-1}}$ denote inducing inputs at layer $\ell$, with corresponding inducing outputs $\vU^{(\ell)} = f^{(\ell)}(\vZ^{(\ell)}) \in \mathbb{R}^{m_\ell \times d_\ell}$. Following from work by @damianou_deep_2013 and @titsias_variational_2009, the variational distribution is able to factorise across layers:

$$
q(\{\vF^{(\ell)}, \vU^{(\ell)}\}_{\ell=1}^L) = \prod_{\ell=1}^{L} p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vU^{(\ell)}, \vF^{(\ell-1)}) q(\vU^{(\ell)}),
$$ {#eq-dgp_variational_factorization}

where $q(\vU^{(\ell)}) = \mathcal{N}(\vU^{(\ell)} \mid \vM^{(\ell)}, \vS^{(\ell)})$ with variational parameters $\vM^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{m_\ell \times d_\ell}$ and covariances $\vS^{(\ell)}$. Rather than placing a variational distribution over each layer's full $n \times d_\ell$ output matrix, we only learn distributions over the much smaller $m_\ell \times d_\ell$ inducing outputs at each layer. The per-layer GP conditional $p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vU^{(\ell)}, \vF^{(\ell-1)})$ then moves information from inducing values to all training points.

The conditional $p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vU^{(\ell)}, \vF^{(\ell-1)})$ uses the GP prior structure. For layer $\ell$ with inputs from the previous layer $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$ and inducing inputs $\vZ^{(\ell)}$:

$$
p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vU^{(\ell)}, \vF^{(\ell-1)}) = \mathcal{N}\left(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid A^{(\ell)} \vU^{(\ell)}, \, K^{(\ell)}_{ff} - A^{(\ell)} K^{(\ell)}_{uu} A^{(\ell)\top}\right),
$$ {#eq-dgp_layer_conditional}

where $A^{(\ell)} = K^{(\ell)}_{fu} (K^{(\ell)}_{uu})^{-1}$. The covariance matrices $K^{(\ell)}_{ff}$, $K^{(\ell)}_{fu}$, and $K^{(\ell)}_{uu}$ depend on the random inputs $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$, creating dependencies across layers.

The ELBO for DGPs is:

$$
\mathcal{L} = \mathbb{E}_{q(\vF^{(1:L)})}[\log p(\vy \mid \vF^{(L)})] - \sum_{\ell=1}^{L} \KL(q(\vU^{(\ell)}) \| p(\vU^{(\ell)})).
$$ {#eq-dgp_elbo}

There is one data-fit term (the expected log-likelihood at the final layer) and one KL regularisation term per layer, which penalises each layer's variational posterior for deviating from its GP prior, just as there is in the standard GP case. The KL terms have closed form since $q(\vU^{(\ell)})$ and $p(\vU^{(\ell)})$ are both Gaussian. However, the expected log-likelihood requires integrating over all the layers outputs $\vF^{(1:L)}$ which has non-Gaussian dependencies across layers and so cannot be easily evaluated.

The expectation in @eq-dgp_elbo involves:

$$
\mathbb{E}_{q}[\log p(\vy \mid \vF^{(L)})] = \int \cdots \int \log p(\vy \mid \vF^{(L)}) \prod_{\ell=1}^{L} q(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vF^{(\ell-1)}) \, d\vF^{(1)} \cdots d\vF^{(L)},
$$ {#eq-dgp_nested_expectation}

where $q(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vF^{(\ell-1)})$ is obtained by integrating out $\vU^{(\ell)}$:

$$
q(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vF^{(\ell-1)}) = \int p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vU^{(\ell)}, \vF^{(\ell-1)}) q(\vU^{(\ell)}) \, d\vU^{(\ell)}.
$$ {#eq-marginal_q_layer}

This integral is Gaussian:

$$
q(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vF^{(\ell-1)}) = \mathcal{N}\left(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid A^{(\ell)} \vM^{(\ell)}, \, K^{(\ell)}_{ff} - A^{(\ell)}(K^{(\ell)}_{uu} - \vS^{(\ell)})A^{(\ell)\top}\right).
$$ {#eq-marginal_q_layer_explicit}

Compared to the GP prior $p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vF^{(\ell-1)}) = \mathcal{N}(\vzero, K^{(\ell)}_{ff})$, this has a non-zero mean (coming from $\vM^{(\ell)}$) and lower variance (the term $A^{(\ell)}(K^{(\ell)}_{uu} - \vS^{(\ell)})A^{(\ell)\top}$ takes off the uncertainty that is explained by the inducing points, then adds back only what $\vS^{(\ell)}$ says is left). While Gaussian in $\vF^{(\ell)}$ when $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$ is fixed, the overall distribution is non-Gaussian because the covariance matrices $K^{(\ell)}$ depend non-linearly on the random $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$.

@damianou_deep_2013 addressed this by further approximating the variational distribution. They introduce variational distributions over the intermediate layer outputs:

$$
q(\vF^{(\ell)}) = \mathcal{N}(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vmu^{(\ell)}, \vSigma^{(\ell)}),
$$ {#eq-damianou_q_F}

treating $\{\vmu^{(\ell)}, \vSigma^{(\ell)}\}$ as additional variational parameters. This "mean-field" approximation breaks the dependencies between layers but introduces $O(nLd)$ additional parameters and loses the structure that $\vF^{(\ell)}$ should be generated from $\vF^{(\ell-1)}$ via a GP.

The resulting ELBO becomes:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{MF}} = \mathbb{E}_{q(\vF^{(L)})}[\log p(\vy \mid \vF^{(L)})] - \sum_{\ell=1}^{L} \mathbb{E}_{q(\vF^{(\ell-1)})}\left[\KL(q(\vF^{(\ell)}) \| p(\vF^{(\ell)} \mid \vF^{(\ell-1)}))\right].
$$ {#eq-damianou_elbo}

This approach enabled the original DGP work but suffers from scalability issues (variational parameters grow with $n$) and may produce poor approximations due to the mean-field assumption of independence between each layer's outputs, which ignores the hierarchical structure of the model.
